- Black specks/dots visible on the exterior stem surface
- The interior pith appears white/light-colored
- The specks appear somewhat linearly arranged on the stem

Top candidates: Diaporthe, Charcoal_Rot, Anthracnose. Let me compare references.

Key comparisons so far:
- **Diaporthe**: Black pycnidia in linear rows on stems, white pith - matches well
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Shows dark brown internal tissue - doesn't match (test image has white pith)
- **Anthracnose**: Dark irregular lesions on pods - different pattern

Let me view a few more references to be thorough.
My initial prediction is **Diaporthe**. The black pycnidia in linear rows on the stem exterior with white internal pith is characteristic. Let me check the confusion guide.

No confusion guide exists for Diaporthe, so it's not a known attractor. The evidence strongly supports this diagnosis.

**Key evidence:**
- Black specks (pycnidia) visible on the exterior of the mature soybean stem, arranged in linear rows
- Internal pith is white/light-colored (rules out Charcoal Rot which has dark microsclerotia internally, and Brown Stem Rot which has brown pith)
- The pycnidia are on the outside of the stem and larger than microsclerotia (rules out Charcoal Rot)
- No fluffy white mycelium (rules out White Mold)
